system.summary: Numerical code to about 3,300, groups separated by dots, heavily homophonic (no group above ~1%), not alphabetical; some groups carry a trailing mark.
system.notes: Not the Dedem 1788-93 code (overlap at chance), nor the Spaen 1808 or Fagel 1804 codes.

prior_solution.where: None found: DECODE, Colenbrander Gedenkstukken V, NA 2.21.008.78 inventory.

conditions.human_role: Posed the target from the catalogue; DECODE account cookie.

solution.what: Fetched both DECODE records, 13 images and the two 2020 transcriptions.
Checked all 13 pages for interlinear, margin or separate decipherment.
Parsed 2,585 groups (931 distinct, to ~3,300); top group ~1%: heavily homophonic, frequent groups spread, not one-part.
Compared group vocabulary with the Dedem 1788-93 cribs R1947, R2053, R2121, R2122: overlap 30-33% vs 28% chance.
DECODE key records, Colenbrander Gedenkstukken V, NA 2.21.008.78 (Röell papers) inventory: no key or decipherment.

Found DECODE's archive number wrong (1.02.04 = Portugal); Turkish legation is NA 1.02.20. Checked its online scans: inv. 804 (1785-93 SG copies), 988 (Röell to Testa 1809-10, clear Dutch, no 9 Feb despatch), 990 (Dedem to Testa, clear French), 980 (Testa to Dedem copies, clear).
French and 'Monsieur' fit Van Dedem to chargé Testa rather than Röell; no clear counterpart found.

outcome.method_basis: No key, decipherment or crib was found for the heavily homophonic code of R1469/R1470 (DECODE, Colenbrander, NA archives checked); group statistics and comparison with the Dedem 1788 code ruled out the known routes.
outcome.notes: Closed from the evidence; needs the codebook or a crib.
